deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a draft table of contents, with one preparatory paragraph, for Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The article numbers 6-18 match the printed dissertation closely. The previous page drafts the Art. 15 argument (vanishing of the first variation N). The next page gives a revised version of Arts. 16-18.

(0) Opening paragraph (geometric interpretation, draft of Arts. 2-3). A continuous function w of a complex variable z, varying in a given two-dimensional domain, is represented geometrically as a relation between two plane surfaces. One covers the region A of the z-plane; the other covers the region B of the w-plane. This relation can be viewed as a mapping of one surface onto the other. The mapping does not change the connectivity ('ohne Änderung des Zusammenhangs') and leaves the smallest parts undistorted, i.e. it is conformal. The printed text says 'Aehnlichkeit in den kleinsten Theilen'. The set of points representing the values of w in plane B forms a surface (sentence broken off).

Art. 6. Connectivity of a surface: simple and multiple connectivity, cross-cuts (Querschnitte).

Art. 7. Green / divergence theorem on the (possibly multi-sheeted) surface T. If X, Y are continuous on T, then
  ∫_T (∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y) dT = −∫_{∂T} (X cos ξ + Y cos η) ds.
Here ξ, η are the angles between the INWARD normal and the x- and y-axes. Implicit step (mine): with outward unit normal n = (−cos ξ, −cos η), this is the usual ∫ div F dT = ∮ F·n ds.

Art. 8. Along any curve, introduce arc length s and normal coordinate p. Their relative signs are fixed by ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p, hence also ∂y/∂s = −∂x/∂p. On the boundary, with p the inward normal, s then runs in the positive (counterclockwise) sense. Art. 7 then reads
  ∫(X_x + Y_y) dT = −∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds.

Art. 9. Application: if X_x + Y_y = 0 throughout T, the boundary integral ∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds vanishes over the whole boundary of any part of T. Consequence (as in the printed text): ∫(X dy − Y dx) between two points is independent of the path in a simply connected region. In a multiply connected region it changes only by periods across cross-cuts.

Art. 10. A function u on a surface T simply covering A which, generally speaking, satisfies Δu = u_xx + u_yy = 0 ('= 0' omitted in the MS), and is finite and continuous with all its derivatives.

Art. 11. Properties of such harmonic functions: mean-value property, no interior extremum, determination by values along a line segment, etc.

Art. 12. Conditions under which, in the interior of a simply connected T simply covering A, a function W of z exists that is finite and continuous with all derivatives everywhere. This amounts to the Cauchy-Riemann equations, with the conjugate built by Art. 9.

Art. 13. Isolated interior discontinuities of such a function: poles, logarithmic terms, Laurent-type expansion.

Art. 14. Extension to interior points of an arbitrary plane surface, including branch points of a multi-sheeted surface.

Art. 15 (Dirichlet principle). For given α, β put
  Ω(α) = ∫_T [(α_x − β_y)² + (α_y + β_x)²] dT.
Vary α by functions λ that vanish on the boundary and are continuous, or discontinuous only at isolated points (finite Dirichlet integral). Claim: Ω attains a minimum for exactly one such modification.
Implicit steps (mine, cf. previous page):
  Ω(α + hλ) = Ω(α) + 2hN + h² ∫(λ_x² + λ_y²) dT,
  N = ∫[(α_x − β_y) λ_x + (α_y + β_x) λ_y] dT.
Uniqueness: the quadratic term is positive unless λ is constant; λ = 0 on the boundary forces λ ≡ 0, up to values at isolated points. At the minimizer ω, N = 0 for all λ. Art. 7 with X = (ω_x − β_y)λ, Y = (ω_y + β_x)λ then gives
  ∂/∂x(ω_x − β_y) + ∂/∂y(ω_y + β_x) = Δω = 0
where the data are smooth.

Interlinear note: 'Zurückführung [?] einiger Punkte, auf denen der Satz des vorigen Art. ...'. Art. 16 then reads 'Begründung/Beseitigung [?] einzelner Punkte des vorigen Art. mittelst der Grenzmethode'. The next page has 'Beweis des im vorigen Art. vorausgesetzten Satzes mittelst der Grenzmethode', i.e. justifying the exceptional isolated points by a limiting process.

Art. 17 (main existence theorem). Let α + βi be given on T with Ω finite over the whole surface. Then it can always, and in only one way, be turned into a function of z by adding a complex quantity λ + μi that is purely imaginary on the boundary (λ = 0 there). This added quantity satisfies certain continuity conditions, and its imaginary part μ has a prescribed value at one point.
Implicit construction (mine, matching the dissertation): take u = α + λ minimizing Ω. Then X = u_x − β_y and Y = u_y + β_x satisfy X_x + Y_y = 0. By Art. 9 define μ through μ_y = X, μ_x = −Y. Then v = β + μ satisfies v_y = u_x and v_x = −u_y, so u + iv is a function of z. μ is fixed up to an additive constant, which the value at one point removes. The next page refines this with cross-cuts T* for multiply connected T.
errors: Art. 10: the Laplace equation is written as ∂²u/∂x² + ∂²u/∂y² without '= 0' (slip of the pen).
Art. 12: the sentence lacks its main verb (e.g. 'existirt'); it is an outline fragment.

Art. 15: the existence of a minimizer is asserted without valid justification. This is the Dirichlet principle as Riemann used it; Weierstrass (1870) showed such a minimum need not be attained. Uniqueness (up to isolated points) is correct. Existence was later justified by Hilbert (1900/1904), or obtained otherwise by Schwarz and Neumann.
Opening paragraph: the description of the map breaks off mid-sentence ('bildet eine Fläche').
Art. 7: stated for X, Y continuous only; differentiability of X, Y (at least piecewise) is tacitly needed for the left side to make sense.

results.what: Geometric interpretation of a complex function as a conformal map between plane surfaces covering regions A and B, preserving connectivity
results.modern_name: Conformal mapping interpretation of holomorphic functions
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (conformality, 1825); Riemann 1851 for the systematic viewpoint

results.what: ∫(X_x+Y_y)dT = −∫(X cos ξ + Y cos η)ds with the inward normal
results.modern_name: Green's theorem / divergence theorem in the plane

results.what: Path independence when the divergence vanishes; harmonic functions and their properties
results.modern_name: Exactness of closed forms / harmonic conjugates; mean value and maximum principles

results.what: Minimization of Ω = ∫((α_x−β_y)²+(α_y+β_x)²)dT over boundary-vanishing variations, with a unique minimizer
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851/1857 (named after Dirichlet; Green, Thomson, Gauss)

results.what: Any α+βi with finite Ω becomes uniquely holomorphic by adding λ+μi with λ=0 on the boundary and μ prescribed at a point
results.modern_name: Riemann's existence theorem (Art. 18 of the dissertation; basis of the Riemann mapping theorem)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a known draft outline of Riemann's 1851 dissertation. Its article structure (connectivity, Green's theorem, s/p coordinates, harmonic functions, Dirichlet principle, existence theorem) matches the printed text, so all content is well known as Riemann's. Minor interest lies only in the drafting stages, e.g. the 'Grenzmethode' article, which was later restructured.

transcription_corrections: Art. 10: the formula should read ∂²u/∂x²+∂²u/∂y² (=0); '=0' is absent in the MS itself, not a transcription loss.
Opening paragraph, 'ohne Veränderung der kleinsten Theile': possibly 'ohne Verzerrung der kleinsten Theile'. The sense is conformality (printed: 'Aehnlichkeit in den kleinsten Theilen').
Art. 16: the first word, transcribed 'Beseitigung', may rather be 'Begründung'. Compare the next page: 'Beweis des im vorigen Art. vorausgesetzten Satzes mittelst der Grenzmethode'.
Interlinear line above Art. 16: the ending 'verl. [?]' plausibly reads 'beruht' ('einiger Punkte, auf denen der Satz des vorigen Art. beruht').
Art. 17: 'welche gewissen für Unstetigkeiten [?] Stetigkeitsbedingungen genügt' is more likely just 'welche gewissen Stetigkeitsbedingungen genügt', with the preceding word deleted.
Marginal 'Art.' marks at 6 and 9, and the bracket spanning 6-9 on the left, are editorial grouping marks by Riemann.
